analysis.investment_thesis: Active Infra is a sub-300 Cr micro-cap civil contractor riding India's infra theme, but revenue dipped from 97 Cr to 90 Cr in FY25, ROE is a modest 13.6%, and at 26x P/E it is not cheaply priced for the execution and cyclical risks involved. Too small and unproven to justify conviction — I would pass and wait for a 2-3 year track record as a listed entity.
key_strengths: Promoter holding strong at 72.38% with skin in the game
Infrastructure tailwind — govt capex and Make-in-India support the sector
Deleveraging: borrowings down from 109 Cr (FY22) to 60 Cr (FY25), aided by equity raise
key_risks: Revenue declined YoY (97→90 Cr) and OCF collapsed from 32 Cr to 5 Cr in FY25
Micro-cap contractor with lumpy project revenue, working capital intensive, no moat
ROE 13.6% / ROCE 15.5% is mediocre; 26x P/E leaves no margin of safety
red_flags: FY25 OCF of 5 Cr vs reported PAT of 13 Cr — quality of earnings worth scrutinising
Large equity infusion in FY25 (reserves 22→108 Cr) on a base with declining topline
Total assets doubled (108→220 Cr) while revenue fell — asset turnover deteriorating
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The India infrastructure story is real and multi-decadal, but you have to pick winners with scale, order-book visibility, and proven execution. Active Infra is a freshly-capitalised 267 Cr micro-cap whose revenue actually contracted 7% in FY25 even as the sector boomed — that is a red flag for me. The balance sheet doubled to 220 Cr post equity raise, yet revenue went the wrong way; asset productivity is declining at precisely the point the market is paying 26x earnings for growth. Operating cash flow crashing from 32 Cr to 5 Cr while reported PAT rose to 13 Cr also suggests receivables or WIP build-up typical of small contractors chasing top-line.

I like the 72% promoter holding and the deleveraging trend, but the fundamentals don't yet earn Jhunjhunwala-style conviction: ROE 13.6% is below my 15%+ hurdle, there is no moat in civil contracting, and the 3-year revenue CAGR is optically inflated by a FY22 base of 1 Cr. At this size and track record I'd rather own a proven mid-cap infra play (L&T, KNR, PNC) than a 267 Cr SME-graduate. Revisit after 2-3 years of consistent 20%+ growth, stable OCF/PAT ratio, and ROE above 18%.
